messages:
Anya (Sales): Quick update — HazelCap POC finished earlier. We ran a sustained 250 qps baseline and a couple of 2x microbursts. p50 looked good (~40ms) but p99 spiked to ~450ms during bursts. They flagged two blockers: multi-AZ failover behavior and KMS latency when using customer-managed keys. Need quick triage and a short one-pager for the customer before the renewal meeting Friday.

Sam (Eng): Can you drop the run artifacts and the exact load profile here? Want to correlate p99 with batch sizes and cold starts.

Anya (Sales): Uploaded the heatmap + traces. Load profile below:
```json
{"phases": [{"duration_s": 600, "qps": 250}, {"duration_s": 60, "qps": 500}, {"duration_s": 120, "qps": 250}], "concurrency_model": "continuous", "request_payload": "chat_turns_avg_ tokens=320"}
```

Sam (Eng): Got it. Quick notes: batching + prefix caching reduced token compute significantly, but we saw p99 spikes on the burst start — looks like GPU cold paths + KV cache warmup. For Dedicated customers, prewarm + warmup traffic smooths that. Also check batching window during bursts; it collapsed into larger batches which increased latency for short requests.

Leo (SRE): Which instance types did you run on? If this is on Dedicated G5-equivalent nodes, set min_replicas=2 per AZ and enable prewarm for the model variant. For Hosted, we can route burst to cheaper model-variants but HazelCap needs quality parity. Network/KMS: customer-managed KMS calls can add ~5-12ms per request depending on zone and key policy — we should quantify with their KMS region.

Morgan (Security): HazelCap sent the vendor questionnaire that asks for HSM attestation, key rotation windows, and audit log retention. For Private we can offer BYOK + KMS integration and provide the audit log export. I'll start filling the questionnaire and flag anything that requires legal signoff.

Anya (Sales): Pricing ask from them: what is the delta if they want 2x burst headroom for 5 mins/day (worst-case)? They want a number to show procurement.

Sam (Eng): Back-of-envelope: for their model/throughput, 2x 5min/day is mostly autoscaling transient capacity. If they're on reserved commit the monthly increase is small (~8-12%). If fully on-demand it could be ~20-25% depending on GPU flavor and prewarm strategy. I can run the cost calc with exact instance types once Leo confirms nodes.

deploy-bot: Load test artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-poc/hazelcap/1819999999/ (heatmap.png, traces.zip, load-profile.json)

Leo (SRE): Confirmed nodes: test ran on dedicated nvidia-gpu-a100-small x3 across 2 AZs. Recommend:
- min_replicas=2 per AZ
- prewarm_count=4 per pool 90s before expected burst
- KV prefix cache enabled with warmup traffic for first N prefixes
I'll update the runbook with commands. Example prewarm curl we used: 
```bash
for i in {1..100}; do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d @sample.json &
done
```

Sam (Eng): I'll draft the one-pager: mitigations (prewarm, min_replicas, prefix cache), quick runbook items, and a cost delta section. Action items: Sam to send ops one-pager + cost calc, Morgan to start the security questionnaire, Leo to update runbook and confirm prewarm scripts.

Anya (Sales): Need the draft by 10am PT tomorrow so I can review before the customer call. Also they asked for an explicit note on expected KMS latency impact in the doc.

Morgan (Security): Noted — I'll include expected KMS latency range and audit log retention options. If they need HSM attestation we'll loop Legal.

Sam (Eng): Will include KMS impact note (measured +5-12ms) and a short mitigation: local ephemeral caching of envelope keys + async attest.

Anya (Sales): Great — thanks all :thumbsup:

Leo (SRE): One more note — recommend adding a small canary route during production rollout to validate p99 under traffic pattern changes. That should catch regressions before full cutover.

Anya (Sales): Perfect. I'll close the loop with HazelCap and circulate the calendar invite for tomorrow's review.
